title: Filtering the employees table by numbers · part 2

steps.title: Keep id <= 4
steps.prompt:
Numbers compare with small symbols:
  > bigger   < smaller   = exactly   != not equal
Keep the rows where id is at most 4.
steps.task: Try typing: SELECT id FROM employees WHERE id <= 4;
hints: Start with SELECT id FROM employees.
Add WHERE after the table name.
The test is id <= 4.
Write: SELECT id FROM employees WHERE id <= 4;
steps.expected_sql: SELECT id FROM employees WHERE id <= 4;
steps.memory_trick: WHERE keeps only the rows that pass the test.

steps.title: Count rows id <= 4
steps.prompt: COUNT(*) counts how many rows survive the filter.
steps.task: Try typing: SELECT count(*) FROM employees WHERE id <= 4;
hints: Start with SELECT count(*).
FROM employees.
Add WHERE id <= 4.
Write: SELECT count(*) FROM employees WHERE id <= 4;
steps.expected_sql: SELECT count(*) FROM employees WHERE id <= 4;
steps.memory_trick: count(*) + WHERE = 'how many pass?'
